narrative: Demand for PL1__M069162C is erratic (CV=0.489) with a statistically significant decreasing trend over the observation window. Lead times are variable (CV=0.671, mean 1.41 days), and lead-time variability dominates 72.6% of the safety stock variance, making supplier reliability the primary risk driver. The (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended with a storage-constrained order quantity of 5,662 units and a 789-unit safety stock, yielding a 56.7% reduction in total annual inventory costs versus the SAP baseline while maintaining the 95% service level.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic demand with variable lead times favours a continuous-review trigger. The binding MOQ and storage cap make a fixed-Q ordering rule more tractable than an (s,S) range policy. EOQ provides the cost-minimising Q subject to capacity.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is the binding constraint, reducing order quantity from the unconstrained EOQ of 13,088 to 5,662 units. This raises ordering frequency from ~20 to the constrained level but preserves service level via the safety stock buffer. If warehouse capacity can be extended, EOQ savings of up to an additional ~$570/year are available.
